newsitem.title: USA: IMC buying Freeport-McMoRan in $800 million deal.
newsitem.headline: IMC buying Freeport-McMoRan in $800 million deal.

text.p: IMC Global Inc. said Monday it agreed to buy Freeport-McMoRan Inc. in a deal worth about $800 million that will solidify IMC Global's dominant position as a global supplier of phosphate fertiliser.
Phosphate fertilisers are used to nourish a wide variety of crops, including corn and soybeans.

Through the acquisition, IMC Global will also take over as majority owner of Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners LP, a Freeport-McMoRan affiliate that makes phosphate fertilisers and animal feed ingredients and mines and sells phosphate rock through IMC-Agrico, a separate joint venture with IMC Global.
The deal also will give IMC Global control of IMC-Agrico.

"This merger will represent a major step in IMC Global's growth strategy and reaffirms our commitment to being the world's leading, low-cost supplier of agricultural products and services," IMC Global President Robert Fowler Jr. said in a statement.

With about 80 percent ownership of the IMC-Agrico venture, IMC Global will be able to make decisions faster on critical issues such as production levels, said Thomas Pasztor, chief spokesman for the Northbrook, Ill.-based company.
"We'll be able to respond much more quickly to market conditions," Pasztor said.

Under the deal, each Freeport-McMoRan Inc. shareholder will receive 0.9 share of IMC Global common stock, plus a warrant to purchase a third of a share of IMC Global common stock if the stock hits $44.50 a share. The warrants expire three years after the merger.

IMC Global stock fell 87.5 cents to $32.875 on the New York Stock Exchange on concerns that the deal will reduce the company's earnings in the short run, industry analysts said. Freeport-McMoRan Inc. shares rose $4.44 to $30.94, also in consolidated trading on the NYSE.
"I do think that it is dilutive (to earnings) in the near term," UBS Securities analyst Ann Kohler said. "Longer-term, I think very favourably of the deal."
IMC said it expects to eliminate most of the short-term negative effects of the deal on earnings per share by shoring up its balance sheet.
The merger is expected to cut general and administrative expenses by at least $33 million a year, a figure that the companies said should rise to $40 million in the next several years.

"The merger of provides an attractive opportunity to save costs while focusing the company on the tremendous potential for our combined businesses," Freeport-McMoRan Inc. President Rene Latiolais said in a statement.

The company also said that Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners will form a new unit to hold its sulphur business and a 58.3 percent interest in sulphur and oil and gas operations located off the Louisiana coast. The new unit will receive IMC Global's 25 percent stake in the operations, known as the Main Pass Block 299.

Shares of the yet-to-be-named unit will be distributed to all Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners holders, including shareholders of Freeport-McMoRan Inc., which owns 51.6 percent of Freeport-McMoRan Resource Partners.
IMC Global and Freeport-McMoRan said they expect to reach a definitive agreement in about 30 days and have agreed to negotiate with each other exclusively through Aug. 31.

Completion of the transaction is also subject to approval by the boards of directors of IMC Global and Freeport McMoRan Inc., and clearance by federal regulators. The companies said they expect the deal to be completed by the end of the year.
